task: Add an explicit read-only reviewer command mode so advisory delegated reviewers can inspect Koala state without being able to write review/lifecycle evidence.
outcome: User launches an advisory reviewer with KOALA_REVIEWER_READONLY=1; if that reviewer tries `koala review_pass_set --storyId=B-xxxx ...`, the terminal prints a clear readonly reviewer error and no review metadata is written, while `koala session_brief` and normal reviewer write mode still work.
facts: B-edca showed a practical pitfall: a reviewer with Bash could prematurely call review_pass_set; Koala caught stale evidence, but the spawn sandbox lacked a mechanical readonly boundary.
CommandPolicy.ownershipClass is already the authoritative command classification table and cli-engine.ts is the single command choke-point.
reviewerWrite commands are intentionally owner-lease exempt for normal Koala reviewers, so readonly reviewer mode must be a separate opt-in layer rather than reclassifying reviewerWrite globally.

INIT reviewers raised seven advisory issues: settle the activation signal, enumerate mutating coverage via ownershipClass, document the contract location, integrate with the owner-lease gate, and test env leakage / missed commands / takeover interactions.
constraints: Do not break normal Koala reviewer flows that must call review_run_start, finding_add, review_pass_set, init_check_set, scope_check_save, or delivery_check_set.
Readonly mode must fail before handler writes and before mutating hooks can run for a blocked command.
No new lifecycle truth source: reuse CommandPolicy.ownershipClass and document the contract in existing role/separation and ownership docs.
Claude Code CLI does implementation; Codex supervises, verifies, and records lifecycle evidence.
